messages:
ria: Quick RFC follow-up: propose an async compatibility harness that runs after ingest. keep a tiny inline preflight (smoke + fingerprint) so fastpath is not blocked. deep checks run in a resumable job.

omar: high level ok. two immediate questions: (1) sampling strategy to bound cost, (2) how to handle runtime-profile mismatches that only show up under specific kv-cache/batch shapes.

ria: sampler idea: stratified weighted sampler N=1200 by seqlen buckets (<=64, 65-256, 257-1024), token-rarity score, and a production-importance weight (recent request frequency). default seed + deterministic buckets so runs are reproducible.

lucy: for runtime parity, harness must run the top-K runtime profiles derived from model metadata (quant, seqlen cap, batch shapes). start with K=3 (most-likely combos). each profile run records per-sample runtime tags so we can map failures to exact profile.

dennis: agree on checkpointing. design: harness job writes progress cursor to model-registry: {model_ver,fingerprint,seed,cursor}. resume picks up cursor and avoids redoing samples. bundle a minimal artifact for repro: model_ref, sampler_seed, cursor, adapter_sha, runtime_profile.

ria: adapter contract change proposal: adapter.check(model_ref) -> ordered list of findings with severity and minimal_repro snippet. stringified entries only. example: "IO_SHAPE_MISMATCH|critical|input: [1,512] -> expected [1,1024]". harness consumes these strings and converts to structured telem downstream.

omar: policy controls: default permissive (defer failures to harness + canary routing), strict_org flag to block full traffic until critical checks pass, and a fastfail param to run critical-only checks when you want a quick gate.

lucy: telemetry: every sample envelope includes sample_id, probe_id, runtime_profile, metric_tags (latency_ms,p99_loss,checksum), and a direct link to repro artifact. send to telem with dedup key. also emit aggregate coverage_score (%) and fail_rate per severity.

dennis: reuse bench infra: submit mini-bench jobs with metadata (samples, runtime_profile, seed). bench workers are already optimized for kernels. harness controller orchestrates matrix runs and aggregates outputs. prevents duplicate infra.

bench-bot: note: bench-orchestrator queues: bench-prod-1 cap=8, bench-spot cap=6. heavy runs may be rate-limited; coordinate with infra.

ria: UX/API: POST /models/:v/harness -> {job_id, eta_estimate}. GET /harness/:job_id -> stream line-delimited findings. include param ?fastfail=true and ?samples=500. CLI wrapper: `ri harness submit --model $M --samples 500 --fastfail`.

omar: cost guardrails: set default budget per-run (gpu_hours=4). if sampler requires more, harness should either (a) run until budget and emit partial coverage, or (b) enqueue extended run with explicit approval. record run_budget_used in registry.

lucy: golden set curation: infra owns default samplers + tooling; product/vertical teams can register curated augmentations (customer-specific probes). keep golden sets small and labelled. also add an auto-pruner that removes stale samples with low signal.

dennis: storage & security: artifacts (model binary refs, sample snippets) encrypted at rest. access control enforced via model-registry ACLs. add a TTL for raw input snippets to reduce exposure.

ria: triage UX: findings should include a minimal_repro snippet and runtime_profile so engineers can reproduce locally with `ri harness repro --example <id>`. store run summary in model-registry: pass/fail, coverage_score, last_harness_ts.

omar: monitoring: create alerts for jump in critical-fail-rate or sudden drop in coverage_score for new models during first 24h. also track false-positive rate by correlating harness findings with production errors.

lucy: implementation plan: (1) RFC update with adapter contract + harness API, (2) sampler prototype + cost estimate, (3) harness controller POC that submits mini-bench jobs and aggregates results, (4) small CLI + registry schema change.

dennis: action owners: ria RFC, omar sampler + cost, lucy harness controller POC, infra to confirm quotas. sync next Tue.

beyond: keep the inline preflight strict enough to catch obvious corruption (missing tensors, manifest mismatch) but lightweight to keep onboarding latency low.

ria: will draft RFC and post link here. tagging infra and security for early review. thanks all.
